item.title: “There’s been good conversations…”: Harry Kane provides key future update amid Man United links
item.description: “There’s been good conversations…”: Harry Kane provides key future update amid Man United links Manchester United may be desperate to sign a proven striker in 2027, but it now appears that one of their priority targets is all but out of reach. The Red Devils’ sufferings this season can be traced to their inability to bolster the attack over the summer. The Premier League giants were scoring goals for fun last campaign after Michael Carrick’s arrival. Benjamin Sesko was very impressive until his unfortunate injury in the final weeks of the season, while Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo enjoyed solid debut campaigns at Old Trafford as well. However, there was a belief that their relaxed schedule – having played one game a week as they were only involved in the Premier League – helped their cause. United eventually secured third place in the league and the general belief was that they would struggle with the rigours of Champions League football. As such, attacking reinforcements were expected before the start of the season, especially a new striker to compete with Sesko given Joshua Zirkzee’s poor form. Among the candidates linked with United for the job was Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane. United long-term admirers of Harry Kane United have had their eyes on Kane since his time with Tottenham Hotspur, and spurned the chance to secure his services in the summer of 2023. The Englishman ended up joining Bayern Munich instead, and has been a revelation at the Allianz Arena. Kane’s exploits with the Bundesliga champions has seen him lift the 2026 Ballon d’Or. The Red Devils will be ruing the decision to opt for Rasmus Hojlund instead of the 33-year-old, because goalscoring remains the team’s bane right now. The Premier League giants have created chances this season, but have lacked a world-class finisher in the team. United need someone who can keep the opposition on their toes and help bring their speedy runners into the game. There is no one better than Kane for the job at the moment, and because his contract with the Bavarians expires next summer, it was believed that United could have a chance to rectify their previous error in 2027. However, the Englishman has now provided a timely update on his future that is likely to pour cold water on the Red Devils’ plans. Kane set for Bayern Munich stay Kane has previously revealed that he is in renewal talks with the German giants. Speaking to the press in the build-up to the Champions League game against Atletico Madrid, the player confirmed that he is very close to committing his future at the Allianz Arena. The English striker said: “I’d say it’s [a] matter of days. There’s been good conversations over this weekend and today as well. I know I keep saying we’re close, but we are extremely close now.” The update will be a big blow for the Red Devils, who desperately need a proven No. 9 in January to get their season back on track. The English giants are 17th in the Premier League table after nine games this season

item.title: West Ham sack head coach Nuno Espirito Santo
item.description: Nuno Espirito Santo took charge of West Ham in September 2025 [Shutterstock] West Ham United have sacked head coach Nuno Espirito Santo after their disappointing start to the Championship season. The 52-year-old has been in charge since September 2025 and oversaw the Hammers' relegation from the Premier League last season. Widely seen as favourites for automatic promotion, the London side are currently eighth in the table, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough. They have won two of their last six games and have lost back-to-back home matches - going down 3-2 to Southampton and then 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday - losses that have seen them drop down from second place. Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also left the club. Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of the side for their Championship trip to Cardiff City on Wednesday night. "Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club's objectives and expectations remain on track," a West Ham United statement read. "West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future. "The process of recruiting a new head coach is already under way." West Ham appoint Nuno after sacking Potter What happens now at relegated West Ham? The decision means West Ham are looking for their fourth permanent manager since David Moyes left the London Stadium in May 2024. His successor Julen Lopetegui was sacked after just six months in charge with the Hammers mid-table having won six of their 20 Premier League matches. He was replaced by former Chelsea and Brighton boss Graham Potter, who oversaw a 14th-placed finish, but was sacked after only eight months in charge with the club 19th in the table. The club opted to stick with former Wolves and Tottenham Hotspur boss Espirito Santo despite him being unable to turn around the club's fortunes. They were relegated at the end of last season after finishing two points behind Spurs. This season had a troubled start for the Hammers - they failed to win any of their first three league matches and were 19th in the table. But a run of four successive wins in the first half of September, where they scored 16 goals and went top of the table, appeared to show they had adapted to the second tier, with a 6-0 win over Wrexham the highlight of the run. But just two league victories have come since - a 6-0 win at nine-man Lincoln City and a 1-0 victory at Swansea City came after draws with London rivals Millwall and QPR. item.title: Dave Portnoy names the NFL team with ‘no apparent weakness’
item.description: Photo by Erica Denhoff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Dave Portnoy has had high praise for the Chicago Bears on the back of their latest win. The Bears were in Monday Night Football action against the Seattle Seahawks, who have struggled this term on the back of a dominant 2025/26. When all was said and done, Chicago came away with a 34-17 win, which included Caleb Williams securing 247 passing yards and one touchdown. Now, Portnoy has come out to suggest the Bears are favourites for the NFC and said that they have ‘no apparent weaknesses’. Dave Portnoy says the Chicago Bears have ‘no apparent weakness’ Taking to X/Twitter, he wrote: “I’m about to fall asleep, but before I do, I am declaring this Bears win the most impressive win of the season. “They got to be the favourite in the NFC. No apparent weaknesses.” After beating the Seahawks, the Bears are now 6-2 for the season, leaving them second in the NFC North behind the Minnesota Vikings who recently saw their unbeaten run come to an end against the Detroit Lions. The Bears are now due to return to the field this weekend when they play host to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers who are 3-5 after Week 8, in which they beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0. item.title: McNamara to succeed Cullen as Leinster head coach
item.description: Noel McNamara will remain with Bordeaux until the end of the season before he returns to Leinster [Getty Images] Noel McNamara will replace Leo Cullen as Leinster's head coach from next season, the Irish province have announced. Cullen said in June that he would leave his role at the end of the current campaign after a trophy-laden 12 years with Leinster. McNamara is currently attack coach at Bordeaux Begles, who defeated Leinster in the Investec Champions Cup final last season. The 43-year-old previously spent five years at Leinster in a number of roles, including Leinster 'A' head coach and as academy manager He joined the Sharks in South Africa in 2021 as attack and backs coach before he took on his current role with Bordeaux in 2023. Since moving to France, he has helped UBB win consecutive Champions Cups and they have twice been runners-up in the Top 14. In May, Leinster were second best as they struggled to deal with Bordeaux's McNamara-led attack in Bilbao as the French side ran out dominant 41-19 winners. McNamara, who also coached Ireland to an Under-20s Six Nations Grand Slam in 2019, said that the job was "one of the most prestigious roles in world rugby". "It is an honour to be given this responsibility," he said. "We have a very exciting season ahead with UBB and I am fully focused on that before moving back to Leinster next summer." Shane Nolan, Leinster's chief executive, said that McNamara was the province's "preferred candidate". "Noel has a long association with the club and emerged as our preferred candidate very early in the process," he said. "His transition into the role will be seamless and we look forward to welcoming him here next July after this season reaches its conclusion." The IRFU's performance director David Humhpreys said that McNarama has a "deep understanding of Irish rugby". "Noel brings a wealth of coaching experience, strong leadership qualities and a proven track record of developing players and coaching successful teams," he said. "I'm looking forward to working with him to ensure Leinster's continued success, while supporting the development of players for the Ireland national team." Since he took over in 2015, Cullen has led Leinster to six league titles and the Champions Cup in 2018, but his side subsequently lost five finals in the competition, including four in the past five years. Cullen to leave Leinster at end of next season

item.title: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo
item.description: West Ham have sacked manager Nuno Espirito Santo following back-to-back defeats in the Championship. The Hammers’ promotion campaign has stalled following the home losses to Southampton and West Brom at the London Stadium, with the club sitting 8th after 13 games. Nuno, who oversaw West Ham’s relegation from the Premier League last season , had been expected to deliver an instant return to the top-flight . A club statement said: “West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect. “Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.” Former West Ham captain Mark Noble, along with Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville, will take temporary charge for Wednesday night’s trip to Cardiff. The club added that the search for a new head coach is underway, with Nuno’s assistant, Rui Pedro Silva, and goalkeeper coach, Rui Barbosa, also departing. “West Ham would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the club, and wish them all the very best for the future,” the club said. Nuno, the former Wolves, Tottenham and Nottingham Forest boss, replaced Graham Potter at the London Stadium in September 2025 and had signed a three-year contract. But the club’s 13-year stay in the top-flight came to an end as they finished 18th and were relegated to the Championship on the final day of the season, with Tottenham staying up instead . West Ham retained the services of captain Jarrod Bowen to boost their promotion bid, while the club also made the Championship record signing of Arne Engels from Celtic for £22m. The Hammers appeared to be on track for a Premier League return when they thrashed Wrexham 6-0 at the start of September, but that has been followed by just two wins in seven games. Fans turned on Nuno following the 2-1 defeat to West Brom on Saturday, as many of the 61,125-capacity crowd turned for the exits before full-time. item.title: Oak Ridge opens winter sports league registration
item.description: The city of Oak Ridge Recreation & Parks Department has opened registration for its 2026-27 winter basketball leagues. Registration for the winter co-ed volleyball league begins Nov. 9. Basketball registration will close Nov. 14. Co-ed volleyball registration will run from Nov. 9 through Dec. 12, according to a city news release. The teen basketball league will be held Saturday mornings and is open to anyone 18 or younger who has not played TSSAA basketball during the 2026-27 school year and is currently enrolled in school. Boys and girls basketball divisions will be offered. Basketball games are scheduled to begin Dec. 10. Co-ed volleyball matches are scheduled to begin Jan. 5 and will be held Tuesday evenings. Interested teams may obtain registration information at the front desk of the Oak Ridge Civic Center or by emailing Matt Reece at mreece@oakridgetn.gov . For more information, call the Recreation Center at 865-425-3450. This article originally appeared on Oakridger: Oak Ridge opens winter sports league registration

item.title: Boy arrested following Bradley Lowery taunt
item.description: Black Cats fan Bradley died at the age of six in 2017 [Press Association] A 14-year-old boy has been arrested on suspicion of a public order offence and subsequently bailed, after a video on social media appeared to show a Coventry City fan taunting opposition Sunderland fans with a photo of Bradley Lowery. Sunderland fan Bradley, who died aged six in 2017 after being diagnosed with a rare childhood cancer, captured the hearts of the football world. The 14-year-old handed himself into West Midlands Police, who said they were investigating the incident. The Sky Blues added they were also investigating the footage from Saturday's Premier League match and Bradley's mother, Gemma, issued an emotional statement. "So much of Bradley's short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face," she posted on Instagram. "To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt." Her "beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate," Lowery said in an update through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, which raises funds and awareness to help and support children with cancer. She added she did not want hatred directing at the teenager involved, but instead wanted him to learn from his actions. A spokesperson for the club said: "Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland [on Saturday]." item.title: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo after poor start to Championship season
item.description: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo after poor start to Championship season West Ham have sacked Nuno Espirito Santo with immediate effect, with the club eighth in the Championship and short of the automatic promotion places. Nuno's final game was Saturday's 3-1 home defeat by West Bromwich Albion, a result that saw the visitors move above West Ham in the table. It followed a 3-2 home loss to Southampton on October 24. Promotion push stalls West Ham were widely expected to bounce straight back to the Premier League after last season's relegation, and Nuno was tasked with leading that return. Instead, the East London club have won only six of their 13 league games, drawing four and losing three. That haul leaves them six points behind leaders Middlesbrough and four adrift of second-placed Swansea City. The Portuguese coach, 52, is not leaving alone. West Ham have confirmed that assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also left the club. "West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect," the club statement said. "Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track. "Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed. "West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future." A reprieve that did not last Nuno arrived on a three-year contract in September 2025, replacing the sacked Graham Potter with West Ham 19th in the Premier League . He was unable to keep them up, and relegation was confirmed on the final day of the season. His position had already come under scrutiny within months of his appointment, but the club opted to keep faith with him in January. Days after relegation was sealed, West Ham issued a statement confirming he would stay on. Before West Ham, Nuno managed Wolverhampton Wanderers, Tottenham Hotspur and Nottingham Forest. Club legend Mark Noble will take temporary charge alongside Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville, with West Ham travelling to Cardiff City on Wednesday night.

item.title: "Antonio was the bigger talent" – Norwegian coach reflects on working with Nusa and Haaland ahead of RB Leipzig vs Man City clash
item.description: "Antonio was the bigger talent" – Norwegian coach reflects on working with Nusa and Haaland ahead of RB Leipzig vs Man City clash Two Norwegian stars go head-to-head on Wednesday night as Antonio Nusa and RB Leipzig welcome Erling Haaland and Manchester City to the Red Bull Arena in the Champions League. Having coached Haaland at Bryne FK and Nusa at Stabæk Fotball, Gaute Larsen knows both players well and has shared some fascinating insights into their formative years ahead of Wednesday’s clash. “I’ve been a professional coach for 35 years, and [Nusa] was one of the most technically gifted and talented players I’ve ever seen,” Larsen, who first watched Nusa play when the Norwegian winger was just 13 or 14, told RB Leipzig’s club media. “Antonio was exceptional on the ball. He had great balance, was a fantastic dribbler and knew when to pass and when to take someone on,” added the 64-year-old. Haaland, meanwhile, had some challenges to overcome on his journey to becoming one of the world’s best strikers. “Erling was very tall and skinny, and he moved a bit like Bambi on ice. At 14 or 15, he didn’t have the same balance or ball control that Antonio had at that age," Larsen explained, admitting that he rated Nusa more highly when comparing the two at the same stage of their development. “When they were both young, Antonio was the bigger talent in my eyes," he stressed. Now in his third season at RB Leipzig, Nusa has taken his attacking output to another level, racking up five goals and seven assists in 13 appearances so far this campaign. “I think we’re only just starting to see the best of Antonio. As he grows in confidence, he’s going to get even better," Larsen said. The coach also praised Nusa’s character, stressing that his qualities extend well beyond the pitch. “Antonio is very down-to-earth, both as a player and as a person. He looks after his friends and family. He’s a role model for young players," he said. Nusa has had at least one goal involvement in each of his last three outings and will be hoping to extend that run against Haaland and Manchester City on Wednesday at 21:00 CEST.

Elsewhere, a former Real Madrid flop will be hoping to make his old employers regret letting him go. Here are five talking points ahead of this week's Champions League action. item.title: Slow start 'toughest' time of Eustace managerial career
item.description: [BBC] Derby County boss John Eustace says the opening three months of the season have been the "toughest" of his managerial career. The Rams are in the relegation places with just one win from 13 Championship games so far this term. The slow start to the season follows a drawn-out and ultimately failed takeover attempt at the club during the summer, compounded by injury woes which have forced a number of key players out of action. Former Blackburn Rovers and Birmingham City boss Eustace, who has come under increasing pressure to keep his job in recent weeks, admits the Rams side he guided to within four points of the play-off places last term are now in a fight to avoid the drop. "It's been the toughest three months, definitely, through recruitment and personnel that are available to us," he told BBC East Midlands Today. "But it's part of the job and I have to get my head around that and try to find solutions." item.title: Dave Portnoy hammers LeBron James for setting wrong example for kids after mid-game sip of wine
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images LeBron James’ viral moment with a Philadelphia 76ers fan has upset Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy. LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers are unstoppable at the moment as they have extended their winning streak to four games and hold a league-best 7-1 record at the moment. The 76ers’ most recent win came against the Chicago Bulls as the host utterly dominated the visitors in a 126-107 result. While it was a terrific result, the thing that has caught the eye of Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy was James’ viral moment with a 76ers fan. Dave Portnoy calls out LeBron James for sipping wine mid-game The 41-year-old forward went viral for his courtside interaction with a fan after crashing into him. Instead of directly returning to the court, James took a sip from the fan’s glass of wine. While most found this hilarious, Portnoy was furious with James and claimed that the 76ers star is setting a bad example for his younger fans. “If anybody else did this, they’d be checked into AA, but because it’s Bron-Bron, SportCenter will do an hour special on it. Who cares [about] the example it sets for kids that you need to be drunk to play sports?” Portnoy stated on X . For what it’s worth, NBA fans didn’t like Portnoy’s comments and called him out for unnecessarily hating on the King. But will that stop Portnoy from taking jabs at James? Most likely not. After all, Portnoy has always been very vocal about his stance against the 4x NBA champion. item.description: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo after poor start to season West Ham sack Nuno Espírito Santo as Championship promotion bid falters West Ham have dismissed Nuno Espírito Santo after a disappointing start to their Championship campaign, with the club turning to an interim coaching team before Wednesday’s visit to Cardiff City. The decision follows a 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion that left West Ham eighth in the table. According to ESPN, they are four points outside the automatic promotion places after relegation from the Premier League last season. Nuno had remained in charge with the responsibility of securing an immediate return to the top flight. That task will now pass to a successor, while Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville take temporary control of the team. Photo IMAGO Nuno departure follows West Brom defeat The weekend loss proved to be Nuno’s final match in charge, bringing an end to a spell that included West Ham’s relegation. Remaining with the manager had offered continuity as the club attempted to rebuild in the Championship. item.title: David Adelman ‘Embarrassed’ After Nuggets Loss to Trail Blazers
item.description: David Adelman Nuggets Getty Denver Nuggets head coach David Adelman said he was “embarrassed” after Denver lost at home to the Portland Trail Blazers. The Nuggets lost 118-110 at home at Ball Arena on Monday night to the Trail Blazers, dropping Denver’s record this season to 3-3. Afterwards, coach Adelman said he was “embarrassed” by the team’s effort in the game, particularly on the glass, as Portland outrebounded Denver 53 to 37. David Adelman Unhappy With Nuggets in Loss to Trail Blazers Speaking to reporters after the game, Adelman couldn’t help but reveal his frustration with his team’s compete level against Portland. “Adelman was ’embarrassed’ by DEN’s effort in the 50/50 rebs tonight. He acknowledged Clingan’s 9 OREB, but pointed out that they had lots of smaller guys crashing too, and the other half occurred because of those mistakes. Ultimately, DEN got their ‘ass kicked’ in that category,” per Nuggets reporter Brendan Vogt . Adelman was “embarrassed” by DEN’s effort in the 50/50 rebs tonight. He acknowledged Clingan’s 9 OREB, but pointed out that they had lots of smaller guys crashing too, and the other half occurred because of those mistakes. Ultimately, DEN got their “ass kicked” in that category — Brendan Vogt (@BrendanVogt) November 3, 2026 David Adelman’s Job Could Be in Jeopardy Given Denver’s mediocre start to the season, the calls for Adelman to lose his job are coming in from Nuggets fans, who are getting tired of seeing their team look sluggish and unprepared, especially at home, where they are just 1-2 this season. The Nuggets have one of the most expensive rosters in the NBA , so there is no way that the team’s ownership group is happy about the product that the team is putting out on the floor at the moment, as Denver’s performances have just been unacceptable for a veteran-laden squad with as many highly paid players as they have on the roster. While it is still obviously very early in the season, Nuggets fans have questioned Adelman’s hiring ever since he was promoted to head coach following the team’s late-season firing of former head coach Mike Malone two years ago. Anytime you have Nikola Jokic on your roster, anything less than an NBA Championship is seen as a disappointment. For many Nuggets fans out there, until the team goes and makes the decision to fire Adelman and bring in someone else to lead the team, they’re going to feel that their team isn’t going to win this year. Ziaire Williams, watching from the other end of the floor, put it more bluntly. "It's crazy, man. The defensive mindset in me is always like, why are they not blitzing him or why are they not doubling? Why are they just letting him walk to his spot and do whatever he wants out there? But they're trying. He just is that good and he just makes it look that easy," Williams said. They did blitz him. Miami threw doubles at him almost every possession, and it didn't matter, because Dončić has turned being trapped into a team asset. The ball left his hands, found the open man, and the open man — Sandro Mamukelashvili, Quentin Grimes, Williams — buried shots. 19 threes from seven different players. F1 says neither the travel advice nor the insurance situation has changed since May, and it's watching events closely, including the U.S. midterm elections. item.title: “Couldn’t Be Prouder” – Alexander Zverev’s Girlfriend Sophia Thomalla Shares Emotional Message As German Receives World No. 1 Trophy In Paris
item.description: Sophia Thomalla (left) and Alexander Zverev (right), © Instagram/sophiathomalla) Alexander Zverev’s girlfriend Sophia Thomalla, the prominent German actress and model, shared an emotional message after Zverev received the World No. 1 trophy ahead of his Paris Masters campaign. According to Thomalla, Zverev is fully deserving of the top ranking in men’s singles tennis, which he secured just days ago by defeating Tallon Griekspoor in Vienna. It’s worth noting that Zverev had already secured the year-end No. 1 ranking prior to his win over Griekspoor. On Monday, Nov. 2, Zverev was presented the World No. 1 trophy by Andrea Gaudenzi, the ATP Chairman, and Cedric Pioline, the tournament director of the Paris Masters. Alexander Zverev was beaten in the Vienna Open semifinals by Alex de Minaur In addition to helping him secure the No. 1 ranking, Zverev’s victory over Griekspoor in Vienna saw the German book a quarterfinal berth at the ATP 500 event. In the last eight, Zverev registered a dominant 6-0, 6-2 win over Arthur Fery of Great Britain. However, his Vienna campaign ended in the semifinals, with top 10 rival Alex de Minaur of Australia edging the German 6-4, 1-6, 7-6(4). The result once again led to scrutiny of Zverev’s No. 1 status, with many fans feeling that he has reached the summit of the rankings primarily because of rivals Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner’s injury issues. At the Paris Masters, Zverev is the top seed and has received a first-round bye. He is set to get his campaign at the year’s last Masters 1000 event underway with a tricky second-round match against former No. 5 Lorenzo Musetti of Italy. Musetti, currently ranked No. 24 and unseeded in Paris, defeated another former top 10 star, Hubert Hurkacz, in the first round. Concerningly for Zverev, the Italian leads their head-to-head 3-2 . item.description: Serena Williams and her sister, Venus Williams, compete in a doubles match during the Cincinnati Open at the Lindner Family Tennis Center in Mason on Aug. 17, 2026. The sisters fell to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns, 6-2, 1-6, 10-8. Venus Williams has hinted at her future in professional tennis. The former World No. 1 and seven-time Major singles champion continues to play despite suffering numerous chastening losses in recent seasons, particularly in singles. Her latest comments about her future came after a shocking first-round loss to 23-year-old compatriot Mary Stoiana, currently ranked outside the WTA top 100. On Monday, November 2, Stoiana delivered a dominant performance to defeat Williams 6-2, 6-3. After the result, which marked Williams’ 17th successive singles loss, the American tennis legend told AFP that she has yet to make concrete plans for her future in the sport. Currently ranked World No. 597 in singles, the 46-year-old said : “I haven’t made any plans for next year, also this year I didn’t make plans, just took it one step at a time.” She went on to mention her sister, Serena Williams, suggesting she could ‘copy’ the 23-time Grand Slam singles champion’s future plans. Williams added: “I’m going to ask what Serena Williams’ doing, probably copy her. We’ve always motivated each other. I’m really fully focused on every one week at a time, and whatever happens will happen, and I don’t have pressure to decide or anything.” Venus Williams’ most recent singles win came in Washington last year To find a singles win for Venus Williams, you have to go back to last year’s WTA 500 tournament in Washington. On that occasion, the former No. 1 delivered a stunning performance, beating compatriot Peyton Stearns 6-3, 6-4. The result made Williams the oldest match-winner on the WTA Tour since Martina Navratilova’s first-round win at the 2004 Wimbledon Championships. After her victory over Stearns, though, Williams has lost back-to-back matches against Magdalena Frech, Jessica Bouzas Maneiro, Karolina Muchova, Magda Linette, Tatjana Maria, Olga Danilovic, Ajla Tomljanovic, Diane Parry, Francesca Jones, Kaitlin Quevedo, Emiliana Arango, Kamilla Rakhimova, Anastasia Potapova, Irina-Camelia Begu, Sofia Kenin, Lilli Tagger, and most recently, Stoiana. According to these fans, events would be better off giving the wildcards to younger players looking for opportunities to shine at WTA Tour-level tournaments. Even though she has picked up victories in the category, her overall win-loss record in women’s doubles so far this year stands at 5-11 ahead of her first-round match partnering Xu Yifan in Hong Kong. item.description: PISCATAWAY – Rutgers football coach Greg Schiano expressed more confidence after his team’s most recent loss that the Scarlet Knights are capable of winning again this season. They pushed Michigan before losing 28-21 to fall to 2-6 in what’s been a difficult, frustrating and disappointing season for Rutgers. The Scarlet Knights have only four games remaining, and at this point nothing is coming easily. Their next chance to pick up a win will come on Saturday, Nov. 7 when they play Wisconsin at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin - a place where the Scarlet Knights have never won previously. Maybe, just maybe, they find a way against a Badgers team that’s enduring struggles of its own. Wisconsin is coming off a blowout 30-0 loss to Iowa, and the Badgers’ second-best win this season – a 24-20 win over then-13 th ranked Penn State back in September – no longer looks quite as good with the Nittany Lions turning in a disappointing season. Although Wisconsin did beat USC convincingly on Oct. 24. The Badgers’ offense has been underwhelming, averaging 318.3 yards per game, which ranks 15 th in the Big Ten. Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph, who was benched against Iowa, is completing just 55.6 percent of his passes. But their defense has been better, allowing just 290.1 yards per game, good for seventh in the conference. So that unit will challenge the Scarlet Knights and quarterback AJ Surace, who completed just three passes (all in the first half) against Michigan. And it remains to be seen if star wide receiver KJ Duff, who left the loss to the Wolverines with an apparent lower-body injury, will play against Wisconsin. This will be another tough game in a tough environment for the Scarlet Knights. Rutgers football schedule: Scarlet Knights' next game Rutgers plays Wisconsin on Saturday, Nov. 7 at Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Wisconsin in their Week 10 game. What time is Rutgers vs. Wisconsin? Kickoff is scheduled for 4:15 ET. What channel is Rutgers vs. Wisconsin? The game will be televised on Big Ten Network. Watch Rutgers vs. Wisconsin live on Fubo (free trial for new subscribers) Rutgers vs. Wisconsin spread Rutgers is a 16.5-point underdog, according to Vegas Insider. Rutgers vs. Wisconsin prediction The Rutgers offense has been underwhelming because of the quarterback play without Dylan Lonergan. His status remains unclear – Schiano said after the Michigan loss that he’s not certain if Lonergan will return this season. Against a solid defense like Wisconsin’s, Surace is going to have his hands full. That’s especially true if Duff isn’t available. The Scarlet Knights’ defense has gotten better, and it should be able to limit a weak Badgers offense. Still, if Rutgers can’t stop Wisconsin on third down – an issue that hurt it badly against Michigan – this could be a long day for Travis Johansen’s unit. This will likely be a relatively low scoring game, but the Badgers pull out the win at home. Score prediction: Wisconsin 24, Rutgers 13

item.title: Can Big Ten spending cap provide level playing field for Purdue football?
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE — Revenue sharing in college athletics is in its second year. For Purdue football it hasn't been the great equalizer that was anticipated. If indeed finances are what's limiting the Boilermakers from winning more games, the resolution comes in the Big Ten's adopted cap . Now, can Purdue get to that $49 million number to at least financially be at an equal playing field to its conference peers? It has been able to fully participate in revenue sharing . NIL income will be a tougher challenge, though some of Purdue's more marketable recent men's basketball players have received national brand endorsements while still in college. The Big Ten Conference, in anticipation of the Protect College Sports Act passing, announced on Oct. 28 that member schools can spend no more than $49 million, combining revenue sharing funds (allotted $21.58 million for the 2026-27 calendar year) and name, image and likeness (NIL) third-party deals. "Purdue has proven in our conversations in the last couple months that we are going to be aggressive and do everything that we can to give our sport teams the backing and the support and the resources that are necessary to be competitive in this conference and then nationally," Purdue football coach Barry Odom said. The $49 million can be distributed however athletic departments see fit, but $5 million must be allocated for women's and Olympic sports, falling in line with the PCSA. A majority of the remainder, likely at every Big Ten school, would be spent on football. item.title: Stumbling block: Wirtz's and Liverpool’s costly struggles against tight defences | Andrew Beasley
item.description: Credit to Arsenal for restricting opportunities at Anfield but Iraola will need his side to learn to unpick low backlines Liverpool did not have a shot on target in their 1-0 defeat by Arsenal on Sunday, according to Opta, the first time they have drawn this type of blank in a Premier League game at Anfield since records began in 2003-04. They did not find the target in a goalless draw at the Emirates Stadium this year either, though in both games they struck the woodwork. The margins tend to be fine when recording statistical outliers. If Alexis Mac Allister’s floated ball from distance into David Raya’s waiting arms had actually counted as a shot, would Andoni Iraola’s side have delivered a markedly better attacking performance? Far more concerning for the Spaniard will be that his team had 52 touches in the Arsenal penalty area (which is good) to create only one Opta‑defined big chance (which is bad). The Premier League average this season is five times more efficient; 10.3 box touches per big chance. Continue reading...

There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
